newsitem.title: USA: IMF-Italy could meet EMU targets in 98.
newsitem.headline: IMF-Italy could meet EMU targets in 98.

text.p: Massimo Russo, special adviser to International Monetary Fund managing director Michael Camdessus, said on Saturday Italy could cut its budget deficit to Maastricht Treaty target levels in 1998.
Speaking at a news conference Russo said, "There is still time to bring the deficit below three percent in 1998."

Russo said that Rome could cut spending in its 1998 budget and there was limited room for higher taxes which could enable Italy to meet the Maastricht goals of budget deficits not exceeding three percent of gross domestic product.

The IMF had said in its World Economic Outlook report that Italy would run a budget deficit equal to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product this year, but that ratio would climb to 4.1 percent next year.
Russo noted that there was a small margin of error in the IMF budget forecasts and that Italy was already close to meeting Maastricht Treaty levels.
European nations will decide in spring of 1998 which countries will be allowed into the first wave of European monetary union, based on their 1997 economic performance and budgets for 1998.
